question: A metrics backend's bill spikes because every exported time series carries a unique session.id, fragmenting cardinality across thousands of short-lived CLI sessions. The team still needs cost and token totals broken down by model. Which change addresses the cardinality problem without losing the model breakdown?
options: A) Switch the Usage API bucket_width parameter from 1h to 1d so the Admin API aggregates sessions before they reach the metrics backend
B) Set OTEL_METRICS_INCLUDE_SESSION_ID=false so session.id is dropped from exported metrics while other attributes like model remain
C) Increase OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_INTERVAL to reduce how often metrics are flushed, which lowers the number of unique series produced
D) Disable the metrics exporter entirely and reconstruct cost and token totals later from the Usage and Cost Admin API
correct_answers: B) Set OTEL_METRICS_INCLUDE_SESSION_ID=false so session.id is dropped from exported metrics while other attributes like model remain
explanations: Incorrect. The Usage and Cost Admin API is a separate, unrelated data source for billing reports; its bucket_width parameter has no effect on the CLI's own OpenTelemetry metrics pipeline or its cardinality.

Correct. This variable specifically controls whether session.id is included as a metric attribute; turning it off removes the high-cardinality dimension while attributes like model, which are needed for the breakdown, are unaffected.

Incorrect. A longer export interval changes how often the same set of time series is flushed, not how many distinct series are created; cardinality is driven by attribute values, not export frequency.

Incorrect. This abandons real-time CLI metrics entirely and substitutes a different, higher-latency data source; it also does not solve the underlying cardinality configuration issue for teams that still want live metrics.
